name: Prescott Bush

summary.text: Prescott Bush was a partner at Brown Brothers Harriman and a director and shareholder of Union Banking Corporation (UBC), a New York bank linked to the German industrialist Fritz Thyssen. On October 20, 1942 the U.S. Alien Property Custodian seized UBC under the Trading with the Enemy Act (Vesting Order 248). Reporting based on the records stresses there is no suggestion Bush was sympathetic to the Nazi cause; the extent to which the American directors beneficially owned their shares is disputed.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: the page places Prescott Bush among the insiders of a 'DuPont, General Motors & Business Plot axis'. No source returned links Bush to DuPont, GM or the 1934 Business Plot; his documented link is to Union Banking Corporation and Thyssen. Treat the page's grouping as unsupported.

Primary records (Vesting Order 248 at the National Archives; Harriman papers at the Library of Congress) were not opened; the Tarpley/Chaitkin biography surfaced by the search is an advocacy work and was not used.
Possible extra connections not written because the ids do not exist: Union Banking Corporation, Brown Brothers Harriman, Fritz Thyssen.
